still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels, and the April 2033 Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India is still in force.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling: 43.5% ever-used − 33.4% current = 10.1% of adults who used and are off now. ~50% of current users are on a second or later course (16.7 points), and 3.0 points have cycled and are off again, so (16.7 + 3.0) / 43.5 ≈ 45.3% of ever-users have cycled. The other 7.1 points stopped once and have not restarted. This is consistent with one-year persistence near one-third on cash weekly/oral products, ~60% inside conditioned tracks and the new Medicare benefit (where missing the 5%-at-26-weeks rule ends coverage), and 36–47% restarting within a year. The 8.9-point rise in ever-use is mostly first courses among Medicare beneficiaries (benefit live Jan 2036), adults in the 14 newly opted-in Medicaid states, and gray-market 'foundry' buyers. Age check: 0.20×20 + 0.33×34 + 0.24×45 + 0.23×32 = 4.0 + 11.22 + 10.8 + 7.36 ≈ 33.4. Income thirds average ~33.3. Users: 33.4% of ~276M adults ≈ 92.2M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~22.0M (24%; ~6.5M of them on the new obesity benefit); Medicaid ~9.2M (10%; ~1.7M on the AUD label, ~3.1M on weight coverage in the 21 opt-in states); commercial ~21.0M (23%; ~13.5M in conditioned tracks); legitimate cash ~28.5M (31%; ~3.6M calm/focus subscribers, ~6.5M indefinite $149 starting-dose users); gray market ~11.5M (12.5%). Sum: 22.0 + 9.2 + 21.0 + 28.5 + 11.5 = 92.2. Public payers cover 31.2M, ~60% of insured users. On-label AUD users ≈ 4.6M (Medicare 1.2, Medicaid 1.7, commercial 0.9, cash 0.8). Never-users: ~19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. They are concentrated in the 29 non-opt-in Medicaid states, among adults with BMI 30–35 and no qualifying comorbidity, and in a self-identified 'unmedicated' minority. Pediatric: 2.0% of under-18s are on a drug; ~3.9% of 12–17s and ~0.5% of 6–11s. Under-12 growth slowed in the 11 states with 'Let Them Grow' laws, where Medicaid children wait 6–10 months for a pediatric endocrinologist. About 6.4M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, and ~31% of US children live with at least one parent on drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~22.0M users): the Medicare Obesity Treatment and Savings Act (Mar 2035) created a Part D obesity benefit from Jan 2036 for BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with a listed comorbidity. Continued coverage requires refill adherence and ≥5% weight loss at 26 weeks. Plans pay no more than a statutory reference price of $245/month net for any covered incretin. Retatrutide is covered only at BMI ≥40. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 22.0M × ~$212 average net/month × 12 ≈ $56.0B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up (up from ~$38.3B). New-benefit cohort: 6.5M × ~$198 × 12 ≈ $15.4B a year. CBO scored the law at $74B over ten years net of assumed offsets, but the first-year run rate alone implies ~$150B gross over a decade. Medicaid (~9.2M): the same law offers 90% federal match for three years to states that cover adult weight-loss use, and 21 states now do (up from 7). AUD coverage remains mandatory under rebate law. FICTIONAL: 9.2M × ~$160 net × 12 ≈ $17.7B, ~78% federal ≈ $13.8B. EPSDT still reaches children 6–11, but state prescriber restrictions limit who can write the prescription.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $3–25 a month in India and 110+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide analogues are $15–50 where patents are not enforced. Canadian generic semaglutide is CAD 40–70 and Brazilian BRL 140–250. India and China still supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume. Exports routed through Vietnam, Turkey and Mexico reach US addresses at ~$80–150.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: in Jan 2035 TrumpRx listed oral amycretin at $299 (down from ~$449 direct) and cut Wegovy pill maintenance from $199 to $179. The $149 starting dose is unchanged. Foundayo $139–209. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $229–279. MariTide $239 direct. Retatrutide $379 cash. Brands hold $150–300 except retatrutide, and access is rationed by Medicare's 5% rule, employer tracks and the 29 non-opt-in Medicaid states. Orals are ~67% of users. Oral amycretin has ~9.5M users, the largest single product. Business Group on Health (Nov 2036): 38% of employers cover weight management, ~70% of them with conditions, and 19% of large employers pay 'steadiness' or AUD-adherence incentives. The gray market regrew from 5.8M to ~11.5M users: ~5.0M buy 'research-use' retatrutide, amycretin and cagrilintide from domestic 'peptide foundries' that synthesise from untariffed amino-acid building blocks ($79–149); ~2.5M use 503A/med-spa 'personalised' compounded blends; ~2.5M buy rerouted imports; ~1.5M use counterfeit pens. The draw is next-gen molecules at a third of brand price, and coverage for people the Medicare and track rules screen out.

GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody muscle adjunct (bimagrumab, restricted label)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder (oral semaglutide / Wegovy pill); the VA/DoD guideline (Jul 2035) names it a first-line pharmacotherapy alongside naltrexone
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide), with growth and eating-disorder monitoring language
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide)

indefinite use of the $149 TrumpRx starting dose (~6.5M people)
gray-market 'reta stacks' and phase-2 amylin analogues sold as research peptides

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity was already reached with oral amycretin (Feb 2034, ~21.5%). In this window the driver is realised through price and coverage, not a new approval: the TrumpRx listing at $299 and the Medicare reference price put the pill within reach of ordinary payers, and orals rose from ~55% to ~67% of users. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. Lilly delayed its tirzepatide dementia 60+ resubmission pending a fracture sub-analysis in women 70+, and nothing was filed. Bimagrumab users ~380k, mostly Medicare high-fracture-risk patients. Implants remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the US market. Phase-2 amylin analogues are not approved but circulate in the gray market. Global incretin market ~$225B (2035). US branded net prices fell ~8% in 2035–36 through the TrumpRx listings and the Medicare reference price.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Medicare's first-year cohort reports higher dehydration-related ED visits in users over 75 during titration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; CMS issued titration-counselling guidance for Part D plans.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Claims in the GI arm passed ~62,000. The first gastroparesis bellwether (Jun 2035, against Lilly) ended in a defence verdict: the jury found persistence after discontinuation not proven. A second, against Novo, hung. Cohort data remain split.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. The MDL judge ordered a joint expert panel on post-discontinuation gastric emptying, due 2037.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; Medicare cholecystectomy volume up modestly in 2036.
No causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. ~15,000 pancreatitis claims are pleaded alongside EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; covered by the Novo settlement framework only where EPI is also documented.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The new Medicare cohort is older and frailer, and early claims show fractures rising in beneficiaries 75+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; the Medicare benefit pays for a baseline DXA; bimagrumab covered for high-risk users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal, including ~4.6M AUD-label users.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA study still puts anhedonia at ~7% of maintenance-dose users vs ~3.5% of controls. A 2036 academic cohort of calm-plan subscribers found ~4.8% at low doses, the first low-dose estimate, but with a self-selected sample.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. California's 2036 ban on mood-claim advertising is the only legal limit on marketing it.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. In the Medicare benefit's first year, beneficiaries who miss the 5%-at-26-weeks rule lose coverage, creating a new cohort of forced stoppers (~0.9M projected for 2036).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; the continuation rule itself produces regain.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency; thiamine deficiency in AUD-label users who keep drinking; low ferritin in adolescent girls; protein-energy shortfall in Medicare users 80+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language; thiamine counselling on the AUD label.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; tirzepatide HR ~1.3. EPI claims reached ~88,000. The first EPI bellwether (Oct 2035, Novo) returned $47M including punitive damages tied to the 2027 elastase signal. In Mar 2036 Novo announced an $8.9B settlement framework covering ~70,000 EPI claims. Total GI-pancreatic claims are ~165,000.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA closed out Novo's Form 483 with a consent agreement on pharmacovigilance reporting. The DOJ civil investigation is still open. EPI wording is on all semaglutide and tirzepatide labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas are still poorly characterised. There are still no data on indefinite starting-dose use, and none on stopping forced by a coverage rule.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric growth and bone postmarketing requirements continue; CMS funded a Medicare cycling registry.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported / foundry product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~44,000. Domestic foundry 'research' retatrutide tested at 40–180% of label strength, with endotoxin found in ~1 in 12 lots. Poison-centre calls are up ~20% from 2034. A Florida med-spa cluster of 38 hypoglycaemia admissions involved a reta/insulin-sensitiser 'stack'.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA and DOJ raided a Tampa foundry (Sep 2035) and issued 60+ warning letters. An import alert covers certain protected amino-acid derivatives. No federal statute changed.

safety_ledger.effect: Unapproved next-gen molecules in gray circulation (phase-2 amylin analogues, triple-agonist analogues)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Perhaps 0.6M people use molecules with fewer than 1,000 human trial exposures. Case reports describe severe nausea, orthostatic hypotension and unexplained elevated liver enzymes.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA safety communication (Feb 2036); no enforcement against buyers.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The semaglutide 6–11 postmarketing data match STEP Young (~0.5 cm/year deficit). Partial catch-up after stopping is confirmed for liraglutide starters. The Swedish ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No REMS. Eleven states now restrict under-12 prescribing to pediatric endocrinologists with a second opinion. CMS reminded states that EPSDT coverage obligations still apply.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~1 per 2,200 person-years in ED-network data, concentrated in the first 8 weeks.

food_and_beverage.state: About 49% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~17% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~14%. The Medicare benefit hit a demographic food firms had counted on: older households' baking, dessert and cereal baskets dropped ~6% in 2036. The 2033 'tariff bounce' in lower-income zips reversed as foundry peptides and Medicaid opt-ins spread. Hershey- and Mondelez-type firms run smaller packs and sell protein lines through Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~22% from 2025 and beer ~15%. VA first-line status and employer AUD incentives cut heavy-drinker volume again. Bardstown/Louisville bourbon job losses are now ~3,100 cumulative, and two mid-size distilleries sold aged stock to Asian buyers. Non-alcoholic and 'calm' drinks ~6% of dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Retirement markets like The Villages and Sarasota saw early-bird checks fall ~9% in 2036 and adopted small-plate menus. Bar revenue keeps falling in the Midwest. QSR value menus hold in non-opt-in states such as Mississippi and Georgia.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Mass retailers run size-down exchange programmes for Medicare-age shoppers. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. A small 'unmedicated' workwear and dress niche grew from Etsy into two regional chains.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. The Medicare benefit's DXA requirement and Medicare Advantage gym benefits fill budget chains with retirees on weekday mornings. Family strength programmes persist in upper-income suburbs.

insurance.state: Part D premiums and MA bids rose again for 2036 on the obesity benefit, and plans manage it through the 5% rule and adherence feeds. Employer pharmacy trend is ~+6%, softened by the reference price, which commercial PBMs now cite in their negotiations. Steadiness incentives are now standard at large logistics, call-centre and hospital employers. State Medicaid budgets in opt-in states face a 2038 cliff when the 90% match falls.

pharma.state: Volume up, net price down. Novo is paying $8.9B on EPI while oral amycretin leads the class in users. Lilly won its first gastroparesis bellwether. Compounders and foundries take a share of the next-gen molecules. Litigation-finance firms are shifting to gastroparesis and Medicare cyclers.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body still reads as your payer. Lifted and scanned means a track. Slow-thin at 70 means the Medicare benefit and a DXA appointment. A sudden regain at 68 means you missed the 26-week number. Fast, ragged loss with no clinic means foundry 'reta' bought by text. A deliberately soft body in plain clothes now carries a meaning too: unmedicated, on purpose.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform. The unmedicated movement tries to join two groups that otherwise don't meet: upper-income 'off-drug lean' parents in Brentwood, Tennessee, and rural and working-class refusers around Knoxville and Boise. Its enamel 'U' pin and hand-written food journals cross both. The 30% premium differential falls on the people who refuse.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Bread Alone claims ~1,600 congregations, and unmedicated households hold open 'second helping' suppers. Retirement communities reorganised dining rooms around small plates. School fights moved from nurses' medication logs to state laws on under-12 prescribing.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps carry 'on AUD treatment', 'calm plan' and now 'unmedicated' tags. Users read 'unmedicated' as a values statement, like 'vegan' in the 2010s, and match on it.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: For most of the insured, appetite is a managed variable and craving a billing code. For the unmedicated movement, appetite is evidence of an unmanaged self. Its slogan, 'Hungry and Here', runs on bumper stickers in East Tennessee. It backed the 'Let Them Grow' state laws but splits over whether to oppose the Medicare benefit its older members use. Fat-acceptance groups still march separately and call it a wellness brand.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Maintenance-dose anhedonia is ~7% vs ~3.5% in controls (FDA). The first low-dose estimate, from a self-selected calm-plan cohort, is ~4.8%. Calm/focus subscribers number ~3.6M, ~40% on the AUD label, and ~1.1M of them have the fee paid or reimbursed by an employer. A benefits-consultancy analysis (2036) found track and steadiness enrollees 2.1× less likely to leave or be terminated within a year. That correlation is mostly selection, but HR departments cite it as an outcome.
interior_life.framing: Employers call it steadiness and 'reduced variability'. Platforms say 'quiet the noise'. Manufacturers say reduced heavy drinking days. Clinicians say dose-related blunting. The unmedicated movement calls it 'the company pill'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: After the EEOC's Nov 2035 opinion letter treated incentives tied to adherence to on-label AUD and metabolic programmes as voluntary wellness within the 30% limit, large logistics, call-centre and hospital employers added 'steady shift' bonuses of $40–120 a month, verified by smart-bottle sync. Job ads in Columbus and Memphis warehouse corridors list 'steadiness-programme eligible' as a perk. Night-shift nurse units in two Texas systems offer calm plans through occupational health. FMCSA remains silent on calm plans.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir and 'dry' stand-up have peaked. Unmedicated folk and 'loud supper' events in Knoxville and Asheville are the new scene. Bar-music venues in Louisville and Columbus keep closing. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The pill window and the bottle sync structure mornings. Couples therapists see the mixed couple, one partner in a steadiness programme and one unmedicated, argue over the premium tier as much as over mood.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Restriction arrived through the states: eleven 'Let Them Grow' laws on under-12 prescribing and California's ban on mood-claim advertising. The same Congress expanded Medicare coverage, so politics now restricts children and subsidises the old. Unmedicated candidates won school-board and county seats in Tennessee and Idaho. There is still no evidence that users vote differently.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal policy is expansive on payment and permissive on approvals, while enforcement against foundries is sporadic. States have begun restricting for the first time: 11 states limit under-12 prescribing, California bans mood-claim advertising for incretins (in litigation on First Amendment grounds), and Texas and Louisiana require an in-person exam before a first telehealth incretin prescription.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Medicare Obesity Treatment and Savings Act (Mar 2035) created a Part D obesity benefit from Jan 2036 with a $245 reference price and the 5%-at-26-weeks rule. It also gives 90% federal Medicaid match for three years to states that cover weight-loss use, and 21 states have opted in. FEHB conditions continue, and the 2027 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper and now public. Part D plans receive refill and weight data to apply the continuation rule, and Medicare's 26-week weigh-in is logged in claims. Employer steadiness bonuses run on smart-bottle feeds. CMS's AUD coding audit expanded to Medicaid telehealth.
state.workforce_or_military: VA/DoD names oral semaglutide first-line for AUD. TRICARE covers it, and the Army recruit oral pilot continues. FMCSA still does not address calm plans.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The Section 232 tariff stands, and the WTO panel is still pending. Indian and Chinese volume reaches US addresses through Vietnam, Turkey and Mexico. Domestic foundries synthesise from untariffed amino-acid derivatives, which an FDA import alert only partly covers. Medicare's reference price favours US- and Denmark-made brands.

events.event: TrumpRx lists Novo's oral amycretin at $299 a month and cuts Wegovy pill maintenance to $179; within a year the tablet becomes the most-used incretin in the country, ahead of every injectable

Congress passes the Medicare Obesity Treatment and Savings Act in a health-extenders package: Part D covers obesity drugs from January 2036 at a $245 reference price with a 5%-at-26-weeks continuation rule, and states get 90% federal match to cover adults; 21 states opt in by late 2036

FDA and DOJ agents raid a Tampa 'peptide foundry' shipping research-labelled retatrutide and phase-2 amylin analogues to 40 states; FDA estimates more than 10 million Americans now use unapproved incretins, nearly double 2034

EEOC opinion letter says premium and pay incentives for adherence to on-label AUD and metabolic programmes are voluntary wellness within the 30% limit; trucking, warehouse and hospital employers roll out 'steady shift' bonuses verified by smart-bottle sync, months after VA/DoD named oral semaglutide first-line for AUD

Five months after a Kentucky jury awards $47 million in the first pancreatic-insufficiency bellwether, Novo announces an $8.9 billion settlement framework for about 70,000 EPI claims; Lilly's gastroparesis defence verdict stands and total GI-pancreatic claims reach 165,000

Tennessee becomes the eleventh state to restrict incretin prescribing for children under 12 to pediatric endocrinologists with a second opinion, signed at a rally of the 'unmedicated' movement in Knoxville; California's ban on mood-claim incretin advertising takes effect the same month amid a platform lawsuit

open_tensions: Medicare is now the default payer, but its 5%-at-26-weeks rule will push roughly 0.9M older beneficiaries off the drug in its first year, into regain and the fracture-prone cycling the ledger already documents. CBO's $74B score looks low against a ~$15B first-year run rate.
Employers now pay workers to stay steady, and the EEOC calls it voluntary. The people paying the 30% differential are increasingly the unmedicated, a movement that now wins local elections.
Federal EPSDT obligates Medicaid to cover semaglutide for 6–11-year-olds, while eleven states restrict who may prescribe it. Poor children in those states wait months, or reach gray telehealth first.

Public expansion and lower brand prices did not shrink the gray market. Domestic foundries now sell molecules with fewer than 1,000 human exposures to more than 10 million people, at a third of the brand price.

prose.headline: One in Three: Medicare Pays, the Boss Pays a Bonus, the Foundry Ships by Text, and the Unmedicated Want to Be Seen
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 one American adult in three takes an incretin drug, about ninety-two million people, and well over two in five have tried one. Most swallow it. The weekly needle that defined the drugs' first decade is now the minority route. The best-selling product in the class is a daily tablet, Novo's oral amycretin. It has cost $299 through TrumpRx since January 2035 and takes off about a fifth of body weight.

The bigger change is who pays. In March 2035 Congress did what it had refused to do for ten years and gave Medicare an obesity benefit. Since January, Part D covers the drugs for people with a BMI of 35, or 30 with a qualifying illness, at a reference price of $245 a month. Beneficiaries keep the coverage only if they fill on time and lose five percent of their weight by week twenty-six. The same law offered states nine federal dollars of every ten to cover working-age adults, and twenty-one states took the offer. Public programmes now pay for about thirty-one million users, three in five of everyone who is insured. Morning gyms in Sarasota fill with retirees there for the scan the benefit requires. The early-bird special shrank to small plates. Part D premiums rose again. In the first year about nine hundred thousand people are expected to miss the week-twenty-six number and lose coverage.

The working-age insured live inside conditions. Thirteen and a half million are in tracks that log every pill. Since the EEOC said in November 2035 that rewarding adherence counts as voluntary wellness, large warehouse, trucking and hospital employers pay 'steady shift' bonuses, synced from the pill bottle. The VA now lists the alcohol-use pill as first-line treatment, and employee assistance programmes hand it out. A consultancy found that people in these programmes are half as likely to lose or leave their jobs. Most of that is who signs up, but HR calls it an outcome. Bourbon country has lost about three thousand jobs.

None of this shrank the gray market. It doubled. The tariff on Indian and Chinese peptides still stands, so the supply came home. Small 'peptide foundries' synthesise retatrutide and unapproved amylin molecules from untaxed raw materials and sell them by text as research chemicals for seventy-nine to a hundred and forty-nine dollars. That is a third of the brand price, and nobody checks your BMI. After the Tampa raid in September 2035 the FDA estimated that more than ten million Americans use drugs no regulator has approved for sale, some with fewer than a thousand human trial exposures.

The litigation peaked. A Kentucky jury gave a woman with pancreatic failure $47 million, partly because of what Novo's safety staff had known in 2027. In March Novo offered $8.9 billion to settle about seventy thousand such claims. Lilly won its first stomach-paralysis trial. About a hundred and sixty-five thousand claims remain on the books in some form.

Against all this a movement with an identity has formed. The unmedicated wear a small enamel U, keep food journals by hand and hold suppers where second helpings are the point. Its centre is East Tennessee and Idaho, its members are both rural refusers and upper-income parents, and its slogan is Hungry and Here. It won school-board seats. It helped pass eleven state laws limiting prescriptions for children under twelve, the last signed at a Knoxville rally in May. Federal rules still require Medicaid to cover those children, so the poorest of them wait months for a specialist. California banned ads that sell the drugs as calm.

From a distance the country is lighter, drier and steadier at work. Up close the pill bottle reports to the employer and the 26-week weigh-in goes into Medicare claims data. The people who refuse the drug pay the higher premium.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Pruitt wakes at 4:10 in Groveport, Ohio. She takes the Wegovy pill with four ounces of water and sets it back in the gray bottle. The cap glows green. Thirty minutes before coffee. She spends them packing her husband's lunch: two hard-boiled eggs, crackers, an apple he won't eat.

Ray is asleep. His retatrutide is in the butter compartment of the fridge, a vial with a printed label that says FOR RESEARCH USE. A guy in Canal Winchester sells them for ninety-nine dollars. Ray's plan dropped him at week twenty-six for losing four percent.

At the distribution centre the screen at the time clock reads STEADY SHIFT ✓ $80. Denise picks four hundred and twelve totes before lunch. In the break room she eats half a turkey wrap and checks her phone. Her sister Carla has posted a photo from Knoxville: a long table, cornbread, a dozen people with small enamel U's on their collars, everyone smiling with their mouths full. Comment: Come down. We have room.

Denise likes it, then unlikes it.

After shift she drives her mother to the Medicare clinic for her twenty-six-week weigh-in. The nurse slides the weight on the scale left, then a little more. Six point one percent. Her mother claps once, quietly, as if at church.

At home Ray is frying onions. He offers her the pan and she shakes her head. It's not that she isn't hungry. It just doesn't feel urgent.

'You're doing the face,' he says.

'What face.'

He turns down the burner. The bottle on the counter glows green.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral amycretin has ~9.5M users, the largest single product.
least_plausible_claims.why: Orals are said to be ~67% of ~92M users (~62M), and ~6.5M of those are indefinite $149 starting-dose users. Oral amycretin at 9.5M being the largest single product fits poorly with that split, and the Wegovy pill alone would plausibly exceed it (mechanism/magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.quote: CBO scored the law at $74B over ten years net of assumed offsets, but the first-year run rate alone implies ~$150B gross over a decade.

A $74B ten-year score, up from ~$41B for the permanent benefit in 2034, is hard to reconcile with that and rests on unspecified offsets (magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.why: Zero state action in 2034 becomes eleven state laws in about two years. The affected group is small (~0.5% of 6–11s) and the movement is newly formed, so the speed of passage is asserted more than shown (mechanism).

rationale.badness: One in three adults is on drug. Adherence conditioning now runs through Medicare's 5%-at-26-weeks rule, employer 'steady shift' bonuses synced from smart bottles, and a 30% premium penalty on refusers. That is far past the 2026 reference, and autonomy scores worst. The public-health ledger carries ~165k GI/EPI claims, rising fractures in the Medicare 75+ cohort, ~0.9M forced stoppers, 10M+ people on unapproved foundry product and children's growth deficits. Offsets are broader access, AUD treatment and a measured low-dose anhedonia estimate, so the world stays below 7. The harms are fairly visible and discussable, which holds epistemic and cohesion in the mid-5s to 6.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Domestic foundries now sell molecules with fewer than 1,000 human exposures to more than 10 million people, at a third of the brand price.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the safety ledger puts use of molecules with under 1,000 human exposures at ~0.6M people. The >10M figure covers all unapproved incretins, including counterfeit and research-labelled versions of approved retatrutide. The tension overstates the number by more than an order of magnitude.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The new Medicare cohort is older and frailer, and early claims show fractures rising in beneficiaries 75+.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the benefit went live in Jan 2036, yet the ledger already reports a fracture rise in its cohort. The fracture signal is documented only after more than 2 years of use and repeated cycling, so this effect appears too early with no causal chain shown.

rationale.badness: Against the 2026 baseline this world keeps every 2034 harm and adds more. One adult in three is on a drug. About 11.5M use gray-market product, with endotoxin in ~1 in 12 foundry lots. There are 165,000 GI/EPI claims and an 8.9B settlement, and pediatric growth deceleration continues. Autonomy is hit hardest: Medicare's 5%-at-26-weeks rule forces ~0.9M off the drug into regain and fracture risk, employers pay 'steady shift' bonuses verified by smart-bottle sync, and the unmedicated pay the 30% premium differential. Some access has widened (21 Medicaid states, Medicare coverage, falling brand prices), which keeps it below 7.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible in fields and events. least_plausible_claims.quote: ~5.0M buy 'research-use' retatrutide, amycretin and cagrilintide from domestic 'peptide foundries' that synthesise from untariffed amino-acid building blocks ($79–149)
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism and magnitude: 5M regular customers within two years implies industrial-scale peptide synthesis and distribution that a single Tampa raid did not disrupt. No capacity or capital chain is shown, and nothing explains why a 40–180% potency spread and endotoxin in 1 in 12 lots did not slow demand.

least_plausible_claims.quote: CBO scored the law at $74B over ten years net of assumed offsets, but the first-year run rate alone implies ~$150B gross over a decade.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the candidate's own arithmetic ($15.4B a year on the new cohort alone) is about double the stated CBO score. It offers only 'assumed offsets' as an explanation, and no offset mechanism is shown. The gap is flagged but left unresolved.

rationale.badness: About one in three adults is on a drug, and surveillance has deepened: Part D refill and weight feeds, smart-bottle bonuses, and coverage that ends if the 5% rule is missed (~0.9M forced stoppers). 11.5M people use gray-market product, with contaminated lots and molecules with under 1,000 human exposures. Fracture rates are rising in the over-75s, children are growing more slowly, and pediatric access depends on state and class. Cohesion strain (the unmedicated movement, the 30% premium on refusers) and thin measurement of anhedonia keep it well above the 2026 baseline. Medicare coverage, a cheaper oral class and AUD benefits stop it reaching the 7–9 range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events (Medicare Act, TrumpRx price cuts, VA/DoD AUD first-line, EPI settlement, Tampa raid, state under-12 laws, EEOC letter). Oral parity is realised through price rather than a new approval, which the rules allow. mechanism: most chains are shown, including the tariff leading to foundries, the 5% rule leading to forced stoppers, and the EEOC letter leading to bonuses. The scale of the foundry segment and the speed of 0 to 11 state laws are thinly supported (claim 2). magnitude: the population, ever-use, age and income figures fall inside the envelope and the cycling and payer-mix sums reconcile. Two failures remain: the oral share against the 'largest product' figure (claim 1) and the CBO score against the run rate (claim 3).
rationale.generativity: The Denise and Ray scenes are concrete: the glowing pill bottle, a fridge vial labelled 'research use', the $80 steady-shift screen, the 26-week weigh-in of her mother, the sister's Knoxville supper and the enamel U pins. Places and institutions (Groveport, Sarasota retirees, Knoxville rallies, Tampa foundry) imply many more scenes. The framing prose explains somewhat more than it shows.
